blogs.title: Beyond the Mucocutaneous Triad: Recognizing Telomere Biology Disorders in Young Adults
blogs.description: This post explores the classic presentation of Dyskeratosis Congenita (oral leukoplakia, nail dystrophy, reticular pigmentation) versus the 'silent' phenotypes often seen in adult-onset Telomere Biology Disorders (TBDs). We will analyze why relying solely on physical exam findings leads to missed diagnoses and discuss how to maintain a high index of suspicion for TBDs in young patients presenting with unexplained multi-system decline.

blogs.title: The PARN Gene Paradox: Why Monoallelic Variants Can Cause Multi-Organ Failure
blogs.description: A deep dive into the genetics of *PARN* mutations. We will clarify the distinction between biallelic *PARN* variants (autosomal recessive DKCB6/Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson) and monoallelic variants (associated with Pulmonary Fibrosis/Bone Marrow Failure). The post will address the clinical tension of managing a patient with a 'Variant of Uncertain Significance' where the genotype-phenotype correlation strongly supports a diagnosis despite ambiguous variant classification.

blogs.title: When Nutritional Deficiencies Mask Genetic Syndromes: The B12-Telomere Interaction
blogs.description: This article discusses the critical pitfall of attributing severe symptoms solely to reversible nutritional deficits. Using this case, we illustrate how severe Vitamin B12 deficiency acted as a 'second hit' on top of an underlying telomere biology disorder, precipitating frank marrow failure and rapid clinical deterioration. We will review strategies for distinguishing simple malabsorption from genetic susceptibility to hematologic stress.

blogs.title: Silent Fibrosis: Hepatic and Pulmonary Manifestations as Hallmarks of Telomere Shortening
blogs.description: Focuses on the extramedullary manifestations of TBDs. While pulmonary fibrosis is increasingly recognized in TBDs, hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis is often overlooked until advanced stages. This post reviews current registry data linking telomere shortening to liver stiffness and cirrhosis, emphasizing the need for routine screening (e.g., elastography) in patients with unexplained cytopenias or interstitial lung disease.

blogs.title: Ineffective Erythropoiesis vs. Autoimmune Hemolysis: Deciphering the Dimorphic Smear
blogs.description: A technical hematology-focused post analyzing the confusion created by this patient's lab profile: dimorphic anemia, positive Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT), and elevated LDH mimicking hemolysis. We will break down why these findings actually represent ineffective erythropoiesis driven by telomere crisis and B12 deficiency, highlighting specific morphological clues (basophilic stippling, Cabot rings) that steer away from autoimmune etiologies.
